title: My AI is currently failing as a stock picker (but is a fantastic researcher)
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
I've been running an experiment since April, testing a large language model's stock picks across four strategies against a rules-based approach that uses well documented stock factors. While still early, the results clearly indicate right now that the rules based approach handily beats the LLM.

Two big reasons standout: I found that the LLM very often latched onto narrative and ignored tried and true stock factors. And it followed instructions too literally, often lacking discretion. While this all might be due to poor methodology, I think the problem runs deeper than that, as this has been [publicly documented](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-06/ai-bots-auditioning-for-wall-street-trading-are-mostly-losing?cmpid=eveus&utm_campaign=eveus&utm_medium=email&utm_source=newsletter&utm_term=260506&utm_content=4208) elsewhere.

On the bright side, frontier models have continued to improve and excel at research, and I'll continue to lean on them for that while pairing those with a rules based engine.

Results so far:

|Strategy|Cumulative Returns as of Sept. 11th - Rules Engine|LLM|
|:-|:-|:-|
||
|Small-Mid Cap Fundamentals|15.5%|5.6%|
|Value|21.0%|16.5%|
|Momentum|2.5%|\-2.2%|
|Blend of Momentum and Fundamentals|11.1%|\-2.3%|

Anyone is welcome to view the [stock picks for each approach](https://app.flexreportfinapi.com/stock-picks) and read more details about the [experiment and methodology](https://app.flexreportfinapi.com/blog/frontier-models-are-no-stock-pickers).

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the momentum row is the most interesting line in that table and i think its the tell. momentum is the most purely mechanical of the four, theres no story to reason about, so its exactly where narrative reasoning has the least to add and the most to subtract. the blend row doing the same thing backs that up.

the confound i'd want ruled out before trusting any of it: the model carries priors about which kinds of narratives paid off, baked in from training. even running forward from april its not picking blind, its picking with a vague sense of how this genre of story tends to end. thats not look ahead exactly but it rhymes, and i have never seen anyone strip it out cleanly.

the other thing that got us was reproducibility. run the same prompt twice, different basket. so when the rules engine wins you know what won, and when the model loses you cant attribute it to anything you can go fix. we ended up only letting models propose candidate rules, never picks, because a rule holds still long enough to be tested.

I've tried to use stock picking as evidence that my data platform works, but, as mentioned in the post, research and portfolio management are not necessarily one in the same, and the research can still be valuable in its own right. 

I've pivoted to spend most of time generating the right research, minus the high token costs, via a [real-time mcp](https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp). The goal is to make research accessible, scalable, and affordable (live demo above).
